provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: high — exploitation of these specific CVEs and SQLi on internet-facing Atlassian/Oracle servers is a strong detection surface: WAF/exploit signatures, anomalous requests to vulnerable endpoints, web-server error/access logs, and post-exploit child processes spawned by the web/app server (java/w3wp spawning cmd) plus version/patch-state monitoring

high — web-shell files (Caterpillar/ASPXSpy-derived JSP, modified file-browser) written into Atlassian/Oracle/IIS web roots are detectable via file-integrity monitoring, web-shell YARA/signature scanning, and anomalous POSTs to newly created server-side script files; the web/app-server process spawning command interpreters is a further high-fidelity signal

medium — command execution spawned by a web/application-server process (java, w3wp, tomcat) is detectable via process-lineage telemetry, but the individual commands are common and need parent-process context
medium — the main-binary-plus-companion-DLL load pattern is observable via module-load (image-load) telemetry when the DLL is unsigned/anomalous, but requires a known-bad DLL or path baseline

medium — an unsigned/unusual companion DLL loaded from the same directory as the Explosive main binary is detectable via image-load and signature-mismatch telemetry, but the RAT does not clearly abuse a signed host binary, so confidence is moderate
medium — ipconfig is benign in isolation; suspicious when spawned by a web-server process in a short recon burst — detectable via command-line + parent-process correlation
medium — whoami executed as a child of a web/app-server process is a recognizable post-exploitation recon signal via process-lineage telemetry
medium — 'net group /domain' spawned by a web-server process is detectable via command-line logging with parent-process context; common admin tool otherwise
medium — host enumeration is common; meaningful mainly inside a web-shell-driven recon burst
medium — file/directory browsing via a web shell is detectable through the web shell's own request patterns and web-server access logs, but blends with legitimate file access absent web-shell context
medium — internal host enumeration is detectable via command-line logging and connection-fanout analytics, but is common admin behavior

medium — keylogging is detectable via API-hook/keyboard-hook behavioral telemetry and the RAT's process/C2 behavior, but the keylogging primitive itself leaves limited discrete host signal without EDR behavioral analytics
medium — screen-capture API usage by an untrusted process is detectable via EDR behavioral telemetry; corroborated by the RAT's distinctive C2, but not high-fidelity on its own
medium — local data collection is common; suspicious mainly via staging patterns and web-shell/RAT process context
medium — credential harvesting/dumping is detectable via process-access to credential stores and known-tool signatures, but the reports do not name the specific dumping tool, lowering fidelity

detection_candidates.technique_name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — pass-the-hash is detectable via NTLM Type-3 logon anomalies and mismatched credential-source analytics, but is subtle and blends with admin activity
medium — PsExec service creation and ADMIN$/C$ access are detectable via remote service-install (Event ID 7045), 5140 share access and Type-3 logons, but PsExec is also legitimately used by admins
medium — internal SMB/admin-share file transfers of executables are detectable via file-write-over-network and share-access telemetry, but require east-west visibility

high — the RAT's HTTP beaconing with a distinctive User-Agent and fixed URI structure to known C2 hosts is a strong network-detection surface via proxy/DNS/IDS signatures and JA3/UA anomaly analytics (exact User-Agent string not asserted here as it was not verifiable from a primary source)
medium — fallback behavior manifests as bursts of failed connections followed by resolution of algorithmic domains, detectable via DNS/NX-domain analytics, but requires baselining
medium — DGA beaconing is detectable via DNS analytics (high-entropy domain names, NXDOMAIN bursts, algorithmic patterns), though generic DGA detection needs tuning to this family

medium — implant self-update pulls executable content from C2/update servers, detectable via proxy file-download + subsequent binary-replacement telemetry when the update endpoints are known/blocklisted

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — vulnerability probing of internet-facing servers happens off-victim at the perimeter and rarely attributes cleanly to this actor; hunt/intel candidate via external attack-surface monitoring and WAF/edge scan-pattern review
low — off-victim internet scanning is not endpoint-observable; intel/hunt candidate only
low — malware development occurs off-victim; intel candidate. Detection lands on the deployed implant's host/network behaviors, not its development

low — adversary domain registration is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via infrastructure tracking and passive DNS. On-victim detection is via resolution/connection to these domains (see C2 techniques)
low — local staging of small espionage artifacts leaves little discrete signal; hunt candidate via file-write telemetry in RAT working directories
low — payload encryption defeats content inspection; detection shifts to metadata/beacon-cadence and known C2 endpoints rather than the encryption itself (hunt-leaning)
low — obfuscation reduces static-signature efficacy; detection relies on behavioral/dynamic analysis rather than the obfuscation itself (hunt-leaning)
low — runtime deobfuscation is internal to the process and hard to observe directly; hunt candidate via memory/behavioral analysis
